name: Elkridge, MD
spotsNotice: All coordinates are APPROXIMATE. Verify access, parking, park hours and posted rules before visiting. Fishing in Maryland requires a license for anglers 16 and older, and a trout stamp to keep trout from non-tidal water.

regulations.summary: Anglers 16 and older need a Maryland fishing license. The Patapsco above Elkridge and the Columbia lakes are non-tidal (non-tidal license, plus a trout stamp to keep trout). Size limits, creel limits and seasons differ by species and water, and they change, so read the current DNR regulations every year.
tips: DNR stocks trout in the Patapsco at Avalon in spring. Check the stocking page to see what was stocked this week.
Patapsco Valley State Park charges a day-use fee at some entrances and closes at sunset.
Northern snakehead are invasive: DNR asks anglers to keep and kill any they catch. It is illegal to move them alive.
Columbia's lakes (Kittamaqundi, Elkhorn) are run by the Columbia Association. Follow posted rules for each lake.

license.tidal: Maryland Chesapeake Bay & Coastal sport fishing license (ages 16+)
license.trout: Maryland trout stamp, to keep trout from non-tidal water

advisories.summary: MDE publishes fish consumption advisories for every county, plus a dedicated chart for the Patapsco River and Baltimore Harbor. The tidal Patapsco below Elkridge flows into the harbor, so check that chart before keeping fish from the lower river.

items.title: Patapsco River / Baltimore Harbor
items.detail: PCBs and other contaminants: limits on how often to eat certain species (especially catfish, carp, white perch and striped bass) from the tidal Patapsco and harbor. Children and women who are or may become pregnant should follow the strictest guidance.

items.title: Howard County lakes & streams
items.detail: MDE's Howard County chart lists recommended meal limits for bass, sunfish and catfish from local waters. Small panfish and stocked trout are usually the safest to keep.

items.title: After heavy rain
items.detail: Stormwater and sewer overflows raise bacteria levels in the Patapsco for a day or two. Avoid wading, wash hands and gear, and cover cuts.

bankSafety: The Patapsco rises fast after storms upstream. If the water turns muddy and starts climbing, get off the rocks.
Rocks along the river are slick. Wear shoes with grip, and don't climb on old dam remains or bridge piers.

spots.name: Patapsco Valley SP: Avalon Area
spots.description: The park's main entrance on the Elkridge side, beside the historic Thomas Viaduct railroad bridge. Long stretches of easy bank along riffles and pools. DNR stocks trout here in spring.
spots.beginnerTip: In spring, drift a Trout Magnet under a small float through the deeper pools right after a stocking. In summer, switch to a green pumpkin Senko for smallmouth along the rocks.

spots.name: Patapsco Valley SP: Glen Artney Area
spots.description: Quieter picnic area just upstream of Avalon, where a small rocky stream tumbles down to the river. Good for walking the bank and trying different pools.
spots.beginnerTip: Fish where the side stream enters the river: food washes in there and fish wait for it.

sources.label: Maryland DNR: Patapsco Valley State Park

spots.name: Patapsco Valley SP: Orange Grove & Swinging Bridge
spots.description: Famous swinging footbridge over the Patapsco, with Cascade Falls a short hike away. Riffles and boulders on both sides hold smallmouth and sunfish.
spots.beginnerTip: Cast upstream and let a small spinner or Trout Magnet tumble back with the current, reeling just fast enough to stay in touch.

spots.name: Former Bloede Dam site
spots.description: Bloede Dam was removed in 2018, reopening the river to migrating herring, shad and eels. The free-flowing water is now classic riffle-and-pool smallmouth habitat.
spots.beginnerTip: In April and May, watch for schools of migrating fish moving upstream. Check DNR rules first: river herring and shad are protected and must be released.
spots.access: Trail from Orange Grove or Ilchester

spots.name: Patapsco Valley SP: Daniels Area
spots.description: Wide, slow pool above Daniels Dam with mill ruins nearby. Calmer water than downstream, good for bass and sunfish. About 20 minutes up the valley.
spots.beginnerTip: The flat water above the dam is great for practicing casts. Try a weightless Senko along the shady bank.

sources.label: Maryland DNR: Patapsco Valley State Park

spots.name: Centennial Lake
spots.description: 54-acre Howard County park lake with a paved loop around it. Lots of shoreline, piers and rental boats in season. A very easy family trip.
spots.beginnerTip: Walk the loop and fish anywhere you see weeds or fallen branches. Worms under a float catch bluegill all summer.

spots.name: Lake Kittamaqundi
spots.description: Downtown Columbia lakefront with a boardwalk, steps to the water, and a path around the lake. Plenty of bass and sunfish close to shore.
spots.beginnerTip: Fish the quieter north end, away from the lakefront crowds. If you catch a snakehead, don't release it. See the Safety page.

spots.name: Lake Elkhorn
spots.description: Columbia's largest lake, with fishing docks and a 2-mile path. Docks give you a clear cast over deeper water.
spots.beginnerTip: From the docks, drop a worm straight down next to the posts: crappie and bluegill hide under them.

photos.caption: Anglers on the Lake Elkhorn docks

spots.name: Savage Park: Little Patuxent River
spots.description: Wooded county park along the Little Patuxent, below historic Savage Mill and the Bollman Truss Bridge. Small river with rocky runs and deeper bends.
spots.beginnerTip: Fish the outside of bends, where the current digs deeper water. A small spinnerbait reeled slowly works well here.
